title: iOS 27 Simulator on x86-64 Linux
summary: Apple's arm64-only iOS 27 Simulator runtime, unmodified, translated to x86-64 on the fly by an embedded JIT (dynarmic) inside Darling. No Mac at runtime. Graphics, input and networking go to native Linux services.
now: Speed 28: dyld_sim's loaded-loader scans run natively (cold Settings 5.05 -> 3.5 s, Health 6.9 -> 5.3, Wallet 3.95 -> 2.86, Maps 6.15 -> 5.1 with the app killed first; first open after boot Settings 5.35 -> 4.15, Health 9.3 -> 7.4). JSC JIT stale code fixed (sys_icache_invalidate reaches the JIT). Huge-page AOT image implemented but the host has no free 2 MB pages. Open: WebContent crash in DOMWrapperWorld::clearWrappers (not JIT), Maps route, Siri UI.

stages.name: 0. Proof of concept
stages.detail: Small arm64 iOS-simulator programs run on x86-64 Linux under dynarmic. 2.45x slower than native x86 overall; calls into native x86 code cost nothing.

stages.name: 1. Inside Darling
stages.detail: Darling's loader hands arm64 programs to the JIT. Apple's own dyld_sim maps the iOS 27 shared cache; libobjc and libswiftCore run translated. System calls go through native x86 libsystem stubs generated from the cache.

stages.name: 2. Boot to the home screen
stages.detail: launchd_sim → daemons → backboardd → SpringBoard, all arm64 under the JIT, software rendering. Fixed: native malloc, signal delivery, per-thread data, tagged pointers, FP16 instructions, thread cleanup, memory-range exhaustion.

stages.name: 3. Fast and lean
stages.detail: Done: shared cache, slim-park, idle CPU, Metal CA home+Settings, openurl/nsurlsessiond, launch breakdown, svc objc_msgSend experiment (opt-in; inlined next). Next: persistent JIT cache, inlined objc_msgSend, Preferences spin, AOT. Speed 3: inline objc_msgSend and a persistent JIT cache are on; boot 71 s, Settings reopen 5 s.

stages.name: 4. Near native
stages.detail: Translate ahead of time, like Rosetta 2, with the JIT as fallback. (1) iOS system libraries: the code that actually runs is recorded and translated once per iOS version. (2) That translation is shared read-only by every iOS process instead of each keeping its own copy: the main lever for under 1 GB per app. (3) Apps are translated when installed, then refined from what runs. (4) Anything missed, or generated at run time (JavaScript JIT), still goes through the JIT and is saved for next time. ASLR is off for the sim's processes only, so translations stay valid.

speed9.notes: Swift timebase patch (X86CODE_A64_SWIFT_TIMEBASE), GetBlock FD probe default (X86CODE_A64_GETBLOCK_FD=0 off), metalhostd guard + on image, prelude sharing (X86CODE_A64_PRELUDE_SHARE), launchd_sim off the image, no .bin autosave with the image (X86CODE_A64_AOT_AUTOSAVE=1 for training), fresh-device IconState seed. Lookups (accounts/followup/profiled) measured: not a boot cost, not stubbed.

speed10.notes: AOT image fast load (map the published .idx: ~300 ms serialized per process -> 1-2 ms), boot-inner cgroup scan without ~35k forks, lf_map 75% load, adaptive gheap refill, image trained on every daemon (25 profiles), A64_CLONE_FROM for fresh devices (home 25 s instead of ~5 min with a SpringBoard relaunch), X86CODE_A64_TIMEBASE=apple (125/3 at the thunks; off: Darling's workqueue manager spins in 8 processes), sampler fixes (GSAMPLE_OUT/ALL). Boot is latency-bound (host ~80% idle); remaining: MTLCompilerService recompiles shaders every boot (11.9 CPU-s), host page-cache misses.

speed19.summary: Native baseline + frame-accurate timing; warm-open latency was SpringBoard bitmap clears through Darling's per-4-byte memset_pattern4; sparse AOT image files

mac_vs_ours_s.note: tap->content (response->content). Mac: trigger = simctl launch (+~0.9 s tool overhead, no touch), warm = app switch. Ours: trigger = touch-down (openurl for Reminders/Contacts), warm = from home, after the fix.

found: Speed 18's Settings 14 s / 7 s were measurement: 2 s OCR polls + the openurl path. Frame-accurate: cold 5.4-6.1 s, warm 1.1 s (now 0.9).
Warm open from home: touch-down highlight at +55 ms, then nothing until +0.83 s while SpringBoard's main thread ran at 100% CPU (12.6k page faults, ~50 MB of new bitmaps).
25% of that thread was Darling's x86 libsystem_platform: bzero/memset = memset_pattern4, which calls memmove once per 4 bytes. Guest fills now bind to glibc memset (X86CODE_A64_FASTFILL=0 restores).
Remaining on tap: libate ASTC encode/decode, vImage conversions, objc retain/release (SpringBoard compresses an image on the CPU at JIT speed).
IOSurfaceQueryTransactionList log lines (8 per frame in backboardd) are Apple's: the simulator build's IOSurfaceClientQueryTransactionList always returns kIOReturnUnsupported.
Apparent dropped Maps taps were a test artifact: a notification permission alert ate the home press.
